It has also been informed that no further additional allocation of food grains will be made to the State under APL and BPL category. The Government of India have conveyed that the present MSP derived rate for rice is Rs.22.54 per Kg. The State has so far been getting 15.15 lakh MT of rice annually under APL category from the Government of India at Rs.8.30 per Kg.

The present monthly offtake of rice under the Public Distribution System, including AAY, is about 3.23 lakh MT. The monthly allotment of rice to the State by the Government of India is 2.96 lakh MT. The additional requirement of rice, over and above the AAY, BPL and APL allocation, was being met through additional allocation of 27,969 MT of rice per month at BPL rate (Rs.5.65 per Kg) by the Government of India up to June, 2016. There has been no additional allocation from July, 2016. The annual expenditure on this pattern of supply is Rs.2,393.30 crore for supply of 38.93 lakh MT of rice.

= Bye

Due to revision of rate by Government of India for rice under APL category, with effect from 1.11.2016, the Government of Tamil Nadu will have to incur an additional expenditure of Rs.2,730.95 crore per year over and above the present expenditure of Rs.2,393.30 crore, if NFSA is not implemented.

5. Taking the above circumstances carefully into consideration, the Government of Tamil Nadu have decided to implement the National Food Security Act, 2013 in Tamil Nadu from 1°t November, 2016. With a view to protect the Universal Public Distribution System which the State has been adopting at present, in which rice is supplied to all rice cardholders without any discrimination, it has been decided to retain and continue the Universal Public Distribution System in Tamil Nadu while implementing NFSA. Therefore, the Government have decided as follows: -

i. Part-II of Vision Tamil Nadu 2023 document on
